text:
joel: Heads-up: onboarding sample app caused a burst of duplicates during token rotation in my local stress run. Many 429s and repeated side-effects.

mai: Can you share a minimal timeline/logs? Sounds like retries lined up after refresh.

joel: Timeline:
12:20:01 outgoing id=req1 auth=token_old
12:20:02 auth refresh started
12:20:02 request got 401 -> SDK queued retry
12:20:02 auth refresh completed -> token_new
12:20:02 SDK retried immediately (no jitter) -> upstream 429
12:20:02 SDK retried again because backoff state was reset -> duplicate created

andre: That matches a parity gap we saw: some SDKs reset backoff on onAuthRefresh resolution. If many clients refresh together, you get a retry storm.

joel: Repro: sample-onboard with TTL=3s and 50 parallel clients. Will attach script to ticket.

mai: Quick mitigations: 1) preserve backoff state across auth refresh in SDKs (parity fix), 2) add small randomized jitter on immediate post-refresh retry (e.g., 25-200ms), 3) recommend adding Idempotency-Key in sample app for create flows.

andre: Agreed. Also add a CI harness test that simulates mass rotation + asserts <1% duplicate side-effects.

ci-bot: CI scheduled: branch "sdk/auth-backoff-parity" will run integration at 2026-06-05T01:00Z.

joel: Filed INFR-8555 with logs + repro. I'll add a tiny harness to the sample app and update README to call out idempotency header.

mai: Small follow-up: please include backoff state in logs (attempt_count/next_delay) to make triage easier.

andre: I'll add a unit test in JS and enable jitter flag default-on. We can tune numbers after staging.

joel: Thanks all, will report results after CI run.
